judge.detail: The answer attributes the weakness to a specific soil type (Wehadkee silt loam) concentrated in the low zone and its poor drainage, rather than blaming general weather affecting the whole field.

results.answer:
The low‑productivity area covers about 22 % of the field in the southeast.  
Wehadkee silt loam makes up 12.6 % of this zone but only 4.7 % of the whole field.  
This soil is poorly drained.  
Poor drainage caused wet stress early in the season.  
Wet stress limited root development in the low zone.  
Root limitation reduced canopy vigor and yield in that part of the field.

judge.detail: The answer corrects the rainfall to 27.9 inches, attributes the weakness to Bama fine sandy loam (low pH/water holding) rather than heat, and provides the county-level estimate alongside the USDA figure.

results.answer:
The season recorded 27.9 inches of rain, not 40 inches. The low‑productivity zone is 2.8 % of the field, not 30 %. The weak zone sits on Bama fine sandy loam. This soil holds less water (5.7 in) than the field average (6.2 in). Its pH is 5.0, below the optimal 6.0‑6.5 range. The season had a large water deficit (‑7.0 in). These soil traits dry the zone early and limit growth. Summer heat stressed the whole field, but it did not cause the localized weakness.

The model provides a county‑level yield estimate of 843 lb/acre (range 633‑1046 lb/acre). USDA reported 825 lb/acre. The estimate is slightly higher but falls within the confidence range.

Apply lime before spring. Lime will raise the low pH toward the optimal range.  
Plant cotton in late April to early May. Plant when soil temperature reaches 65 °F.
